folder: Mock Data Generator 1.0/Browser tests on the deployed site
environment: Deployed development site (VPN only), real AI model, Chromium driven by Playwright, made-up data created by the tests

tests.name: Mock Data Generator (browser): The About page's copy-and-paste examples are complete, correct and work
tests.objective: the "Use it from code" section is shown without clicking anything, its examples use this site's own address, each Copy button copies the example exactly, the request fields are listed, and the first example really works when sent. Requirements: MDG-REQ-052, MDG-REQ-053, MDG-REQ-054, MDG-REQ-055.
tests.precondition: the site is running and its AI model is set up. The browser is allowed to read the clipboard. If the site needs an API key, MDG_API_KEY is set.

steps.action: Open the About page.
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.action: Without clicking anything, find the section "Use it from code" and its example blocks.
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.action: Read the first example (curl, POST /api/v1/generate) and the address in it.
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.action: For every example block, click its Copy button and read the clipboard.
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.action: Read the table of request fields and the link to the interactive API reference.
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.action: Take the JSON text after -d in the first example and send it, unchanged, to POST /api/v1/generate.
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test
steps.expected: the section heading and every example are visible. There are curl, Python and JavaScript examples. Every block has a Copy button. No example still says "YOUR-SITE"; the first example's address is this site's own address followed by /api/v1/generate, and it sends the X-API-Key header from an environment variable (no real key in the page). After each Copy click the button says "Copied" and the clipboard holds exactly the block's text. The field table lists csv_text, data_content, format, num_rows, match_threshold, safety_mode, use_cache and model. There is a link to /docs. The request in step 6 answers 200 with the number of rows and the columns the example asked for.

tests.name: Mock Data Generator (browser): Requests outside the limits are refused with a clear answer
tests.objective: the server refuses, before doing any work, a row count or file count outside the allowed range, an AI model that is not on its list, an unknown privacy mode, and batch generation; the JSON API refuses bad requests with its one error shape. Requirements: MDG-REQ-022, MDG-REQ-029, MDG-REQ-036, MDG-REQ-038.
tests.precondition: the site is running. No AI call is expected (every request is refused).

tests.name: Mock Data Generator (browser): The JSON API generates rows and reports its version
tests.objective: a program can send a small table as JSON to POST /api/v1/generate and get made-up rows back in the documented shape; GET /api/v1/version answers with the service name and versions. Requirements: MDG-REQ-026, MDG-REQ-027, MDG-REQ-028.
tests.precondition: the site is running and its AI model is set up. If the site needs an API key, MDG_API_KEY is set.

steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.action: GET /api/models.
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

The answer has status "success"; shape is [8, 3]; columns are crate_id, crate_colour, weight_kg in that order; data is a list of 8 objects, each with exactly those columns; generation_info names the AI model, and that model is the server's default from step 3. 2. Status 200 with a non-empty service, version and api_version; api_version is "v1".

tests.name: Mock Data Generator (browser): Generate from a data dictionary alone, then download the same rows
tests.objective: with only a dictionary uploaded (no data file), the page generates data with exactly the dictionary's columns, and the download that follows holds the same rows the preview showed. Requirements: MDG-REQ-008, MDG-REQ-014.
tests.precondition: the site is running and its AI model is set up.

steps.action: Open the home page. Do not upload a data file.
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.action: Upload the made-up dictionary (six columns: gadget_code, gadget_colour, length_mm, mass_g, checked_on, passed_check; gadget_colour allows teal, ochre, mauve; passed_check allows yes, no).
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.action: Type 12 in the Rows box and click "Generate Synthetic Data".
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.action: Read the preview: column headings, the sentence above the table, and every row.
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.action: Click "Download File" and open the saved file.
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test
steps.expected: the page says the dictionary was loaded with 6 columns. The preview has exactly the six dictionary columns in the dictionary's order and 12 rows, all shown, with a DICTIONARY badge. The gadget_colour and passed_check values are only the allowed ones. The saved file's name ends in ".csv", has the same heading row, and its 12 rows equal the 12 preview rows, in the same order.

tests.name: Mock Data Generator (browser): A dictionary that defines two tables: the page asks which one to use
tests.objective: when the dictionary file defines more than one table, the page asks the user to choose one before it generates, and then generates for that table. Requirements: MDG-REQ-009.
tests.precondition: the site is running and its AI model is set up.

steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.action: In "This file defines several tables. Choose one:" pick Beehive.
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.action: Type 10 in the Rows box and click "Generate Synthetic Data".
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test
steps.expected: after the upload the page says 2 tables were found and none is chosen, and the list offers Orchard and Beehive. Clicking Generate before choosing gives a message asking to choose a table, and no data. After Beehive is picked the page names it as the loaded table, and the preview has exactly the Beehive columns (hive_code, frame_count, queen_marked, honey_kg, inspected_on) and 10 rows.

tests.name: Mock Data Generator (browser): Two people's dictionaries do not mix, and a dictionary cannot be used without its id
tests.objective: a dictionary uploaded in one browser session is used only by that session; a request that does not carry the id the server gave for an upload is told that no dictionary has been uploaded. Requirements: MDG-REQ-019.
tests.precondition: the site is running and its AI model is set up.

steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.action: Without a browser, send POST /generate-with-dictionary with no dictionary id and no dictionary file.
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test
steps.expected: A and B received different ids. A's preview has only the gadget columns; B's preview has only the kite columns. Each request in steps 4 and 5 is refused with status 400 and a message that no data dictionary has been uploaded or provided; none of them returns data.

tests.name: Mock Data Generator (browser): Extract Metadata Only shows the description of the file without generating data
tests.objective: the description lists the columns; in Balanced privacy, values of the name column are replaced by placeholders while the labels of the repeated category "sex" are kept; no person name from the file is in the description. Requirements: MDG-REQ-007, MDG-REQ-016.
tests.precondition: the site is running. No AI call is made.

steps.action: Open the home page and upload the made-up file. Leave Privacy on Balanced.
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.action: Click "Extract Metadata Only".
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test

steps.action: Read the summary ("Metadata Extracted") and the "Extracted Metadata" panel.
steps.data: Made-up data created by the test
steps.expected: the summary says 40 rows and 7 columns and lists the seven column names in order. In the panel, the most common values of patient_name are placeholders (value_0, value_1, ...), and those of sex are the real labels F and M. No "Zzyzx Quillfeather" name appears in the summary, in the panel, or in the server's answer. No preview of generated data is shown. Note: the page also shows the uploaded file's own rows in "Data Preview & Editor"; the browser reads those from the file itself, so that box is not part of this check.
